absent: Locking and concurrency rules for the committed batch global and its readers.
Definitions and behavior of total RAM, CPU count, overcommit policy values and sysctl handling.
Memblock region iteration, mirror and hotpluggable classification, and frame range helpers.
Full layouts of zone, node, page, folio, device map and alternate map structures.
Hotplug notifier priority ordering, registration failure handling and chain semantics.
Sysfs object lifetime, cleanup and error paths beyond creation failure.
Deferred page initialization mechanism and consumers of the deferred start marker.
Hash distribution consumers and effects on allocation placement.
Movable zone anchor consumers and runtime enforcement of mobility boundaries.
Device memory type meanings and driver allocator interactions.

findings.text: Committed memory batch global and its recomputation routine are visible beyond early init so boot and hotplug paths can refresh sizing from the current overcommit policy.
Device zone memory map initializer is externally visible for device memory setup using owning zone, start frame, page count and device map.

Boot batch setup computes sizing once from the current overcommit setting and registers a memory hotplug observer at a dedicated priority. The observer refreshes sizing on online and offline events, ignores other events, and always reports successful handling.
Early memory sysfs setup creates a child object for memory management under the kernel object. Creation failure is reported as memory exhaustion, otherwise setup reports success.

Boot frame to node lookup cache holds last_start, last_end and last_nid describing the cached interval and its node result. A single static early instance retains the most recent range during initialization.

Boot retains per zone lowest and highest possible frames, per node movable start, requested kernel and movable core sizes in absolute and percent forms, total and kernel page counters, a deferred structure flag, per CPU boot node statistics, and a mirrored kernel core request flag. These reside in init time storage and seed later zone layout.

Core size command line parsing accepts a percent suffix or a byte size. Percent input is stored as a percentage after a sanity check for oversized values, while byte input is converted to pages and clears the percent field. Missing input is rejected as invalid.

Kernel core option recognizes a mirror keyword that enables mirrored kernel memory handling and bypasses numeric parsing, otherwise it delegates to shared core parsing with kernel core storage. Movable core option always delegates to shared parsing with movable core storage.
Early total page accounting sums lengths of all memory frame intervals and marks each encountered node as having memory. The returned total feeds later proportional core calculations.
Movable anchor selection scans zones from highest to lowest, skipping the movable zone itself, and picks the highest zone spanning a nonempty interval. Initialization requires such a zone to exist.

Per node movable start computation uses exclusive configuration modes with a common aligned output. Hotpluggable node mode derives each start from the lowest hotpluggable region. Mirror mode derives it from the lowest non mirrored region above low memory when mirror memory exists and crash capture is inactive. Otherwise requested core amounts are normalized from percent, rounded and capped, then spread evenly across memory nodes with iterative rebalancing until kernel demand is met or no further spreading is possible. All starts are aligned to maximum order granularity and cleared when reaching the node end, and the incoming memory node mask is restored.

Hash distribution across nodes defaults from build configuration and can be overridden by a boolean boot parameter. One build variant disables distribution when only a single memory node exists, while an alternate variant leaves the setting unchanged.

Pageblock type initialization covers a frame interval at pageblock granularity, allowing a per block scratch override of the requested mobility type. Long non atomic runs yield the processor at section boundaries.
Deferred range setup has two build variants. One marks the node as having no deferred start by storing the maximum frame value, while the other performs no action.
Unavailable range handling initializes each valid page in a gap with zone and node association and marks it reserved, then reports node, zone name and count when any page was processed.

Memory map construction clamps each memory interval to the owning zone before initializing its pages with early context and movable mobility, filling any preceding gap as unavailable and tracking the high water hole. The top level walk visits every memory interval across populated zones, preserves the last zone identity, and seals the trailing hole up to section or maximum order alignment within that zone.

Device page early setup performs generic page initialization for the given frame, zone and node, marks the page reserved pending onlining, links it to its device address map with cleared private data, and leaves generic types with default counting while zeroing the count for private, coherent, filesystem DAX and peer to peer variants that manage their own allocation.

Device map sizing selects either the map provided compound span or a reserve derived span depending on early section status and optimization support. Compound construction designates a head and links trailing pages as tails of the map shift order with zeroed counts. Zone device initialization validates its map and zone, skips the alternate map reservation, processes the range in compound strides with periodic yielding on section alignment, marks the whole range movable, and logs page count and elapsed time.

Movable aware zone clipping only acts when the node has a movable start. It sizes the movable zone from that start up to the movable anchor limit, truncates an overlapping lower zone at the start, and empties any range fully inside movable space.

Zone and node accounting derives each zone extent by clamping the node interval to architectural limits plus movable adjustment, then subtracting absent pages to obtain present pages. Empty zones report no absent pages and get a zero start. Memoryless nodes are cleared to zero totals with a diagnostic. Kernel versus total counters accumulate over free ranges with high memory exclusion where applicable. Node totals sum present pages across zones.

Initialization guards malformed configuration and misuse. Oversized percent or page count overflow triggers a warning while still recording the value. Absence of any usable zone triggers a fatal consistency check. Device map initialization warns and aborts when the map is missing or the target zone is not the device zone.
The committed batch global starts at value 32 before any recomputation.

Batch resizing enforces a lower bound derived from CPU count and a large upper cap. Strict no overcommit policy uses a far smaller memory fraction than permissive policies to reduce contention on the committed memory counter.
Strict no overcommit sizing divides memory per CPU by 256 while other policies divide by 4, both capped at the maximum signed integer.
